decisions.reason: Drops the repeated “My mother was wearing,” so the following “My mother.” lands; “printed with” is tighter than the calque.
“Her surprise quickly turned” avoids the translationese “surprised expression” without losing 곧 당혹감으로.
“Flashed” matches 씩 웃어, and “Just then” is the natural 그때 beat.
“Kim ajumma’s son” is the spoken English for 김씨 아줌마 아들; [^1] is correct because ajumma appears first.
Simple past is cleaner novelistic English for the same wary once-over.
SOL adds unsupported “exactly”; “I already knew” already covers 정체를 알고.
Keeps 괜한 헛기침 as an unnecessary cough; SOL’s “cleared her throat awkwardly” loses 괜한 and weakens 허리까지 숙이는.
사장인 내 기분은 is first-person owner feelings; BASE role-swaps him into the owner, SOL makes her speak of herself in the third person.
decisions.replacement: “Maybe it’s because you’re young, but you’re awfully thoughtless. If someone showed up out of the blue like this, how do you think I’d feel as the owner?”

decisions.reason: 기분 나쁘시겠죠 is honorific “you’d be upset,” not Taekyung imagining himself as owner.
말도 없이 is “without saying a word,” not the broader “without warning.”
“What’s with this kid?” is the natural English for 이 자식 뭐지?
잡아당겼다 is pull, not grab; SOL’s “tugged … by the arm” is the right action but an awkward collocation.
decisions.replacement: Ignoring her confused reaction, I pulled my mother by the arm.

decisions.reason: Preserves 물었다; SOL’s “gave them an innocent look” drops the asking.
“I meant every word” is spoken English for 진심입니다, and present “have every right” matches 그럴 수 있죠.
내려앉았다 is “descended”; BASE adds “over the restaurant,” which this line does not have.
“Stared blankly at me” plus a period is cleaner leading into the next-paragraph shriek.
누구 맘대로 is a general “who said you could,” not the extra-specific “who says she can quit.”
“We did” answers 누구 맘대로; SOL’s “We do” only fits the over-specified quit line.
이, 이! is a hard stutter with no trailing ellipsis.
삼, 삼! 사, 사! is clean counting off 이; BASE’s T-/F- stutters are invented English and bury the number joke.
Keeps the vocative 야; SOL drops “Hey.”
“Her vicious curse” keeps the owner as agent; “the vicious curse” is needlessly impersonal.
덥석 is a grab beat; deleting the sfx loses the physical hit.
Keeps 단번에, 한 사람, and 눈을 부릅떴다; SOL’s “a hand shot out” adds a motion and drops the delayed person and glare.
BASE’s “spat … with an aura” is clumsy; SOL’s glare-and-radiate drops 씹어뱉었다.
decisions.replacement: My mother spat the words out, radiating an aura fierce enough to make even a First Rate master flinch.

decisions.reason: 홀에 있을 때 is when he was in the dining area, not hearing “from” it.
달려드는 is a charge, not a lunge; 가로막았다 is stepping between them, and BASE’s “in front of her” is ambiguous.
decisions.replacement: The owner charged at my mother, but I stepped between them.

decisions.reason: Keeps 팔을 휘두르기 and 괴성; SOL’s “flailing” and “shriek” drop the arms and soften the howl.
The line names 공격, which the next thought mocks; SOL’s “none of it” blunts that setup.
“Even call that an attack” captures 부르기도 and reads as natural thought-voice.
Uses binding 근맥 → Sinews and Meridians; BASE’s “tendons” violates the glossary, and the fly-wing comparison is at least as faithful.
Same facts in cleaner two-sentence prose instead of a heavy semicolon.
헌터라는 놈 is “Hunter bastard”; SOL’s “you call yourself a Hunter” adds a so-called reading and drops 놈.
뇌구조 is “brain,” the joke; “mind” genericizes it.
Dropped “that” and the comma make the outburst more spoken without changing the injury claim.
부들부들 is trembling/quivering more than generic shaking.
질린 얼굴 is fed-up/disgusted, not exhausted; “staff” is the natural restaurant word.
딱 좋네 is present “that works out nicely,” tighter than “should work out.”
헌터 때문에 is injured because of a Hunter; SOL makes the Hunter the direct agent of the injury.
시간이 아까워진다 is feeling the time is wasted, not merely slipping away.
심보 좀 곱게 is a better attitude/disposition, not “being a better person.”
입꼬리가 비틀렸다 is the mouth-corners twisting; BASE conflates that with a generic twisted face and “crooked her lips.”
말하면 압니까 is “would you even know if I told you,” not “would it mean anything.”
“My son would” is the natural ellipsis answering that question; 내 아들이 알지 does not need “know” restated.
한두 다리 is degrees of separation, and 소문 안 좋게 is a bad reputation; SOL’s “word gets around” drops 안 좋게.
오래 버틸 겁니다 is confident “I’ll last”; SOL’s “probably” weakens it.
유명할 텐데 is a bragging “must be famous”; SOL’s “should be” can read as mere obligation.
Period is the right close when the quoted reply is its own paragraph.
Goshiwon is the second footnote once ajumma is [^1].
벌이 is income, not “business”; SOL’s “pathetic” over-intensifies 시원찮아.
decisions.replacement: “Pfft, a goshiwon? I suppose that’s the level you’d expect from an F-rank Hunter. Is your income really that bad?”

decisions.reason: “Judged everything according to their own common sense” is natural English for 자신이 가진 상식에서 모든 판단.
못 들었어? is “didn’t you hear,” not “did you hear.”
“Even the kitchen staff” captures 물론이고 … 직원들도; “staff” is better than “employees.”
“About that” is filler; 아까부터 궁금했는데 is already “I’ve been wondering.”
너무 높아서 당황스러워 is stunned/taken aback because it’s high; BASE invents “too high to believe.”
“I thought” is the natural past for 알았네; “had thought” is over-pluperfect.
피식피식 비웃음 is derisive chuckles/snickers; SOL adds “quiet” and upgrades them to laughs.
D급은 돼야 is “you have to be D-rank,” not a description of the kind of person her son is.
말도 잘했고 is “I spoke just fine”; SOL’s “told people” adds an object the Korean does not.
생각하는데 is “I think,” not “I agree”; the trap still works as his stated opinion.
“Slow about updating your information” is tighter, spoken English for 정보 업데이트가 많이 느리시네.
썼어요 is “used,” 황동색 is brass-colored, and 하급 헌터들은 황동색 is have, not “carry/get.”
터져 나왔다 is erupted; “broke out” is milder and merely different.
반전된 분위기 “flipped” is the natural English; “reversed” is stiffer.
이게 말이야, 방구야 is the words-or-a-fart joke; BASE replaces it with generic logic.
“Laugh hollowly” is more direct than “give a hollow laugh” for 헛웃음.
Keeps 사람이 직급 and the binding 대리 → Assistant Manager capitalization.
자리 옮기지 plus the 백반집 means leaving, not changing tables in-house; also matches Assistant Manager and 중소기업 “company.”
그게 아니고요 is a meaning backpedal, not “that’s not what happened.”
Preserves 저희도 as “we’re leaving too”; BASE drops 도.
“Like the receding tide” is the compact English for 썰물처럼.
“Barely a minute later” is cleaner English for 1분 남짓한 시간이 흐르자.
Keeps 망하는 소리, the sound of the place going under; SOL drops 소리.
시라고요 quotes the owner: which Guild she said, not which Guild the son said.
Preserves the 어쩐 일로 echo as “What do you mean, what is it?” which BASE omits.
보내 드렸는데요 is contrastive “though”; SOL drops that protest.
그거 확인했지 is “I checked that,” pointing at the 40억.
이어지는 대화 needs no added “entire.”
눈이 툭 튀어나온다 is eyes popping, and 쏟아지는 시선 is stares, not generic attention.
처음 듣는 이름인데 is “first I’ve heard of him/that name,” not the flatter “Never heard of him.”
“Don’t even know him” plus “Apparently” is natural English for 그것도 몰라 and hearsay 래.
“How am I supposed to know” matches the defensive 제가 어떻게 압니까 better than the flatter “would I.”
받아 놓은 게 is getting/receiving the card, not “taking” it.
Period is the right close when the quoted question is the next paragraph.
팀장이에요 is a Team Leader, not uniquely “the” Team Leader; “Put simply” matches 쉽게 말하면.
이제 가요 includes “now”; SOL drops 이제.
그럴까? in warm agreement is “Shall we,” not the more hesitant “Should we.”
SOL gets 부모면 부모답게 똑바로 살아; BASE keeps 함부로 입에 담아. Each version only solves half.
decisions.replacement: “If you’re a parent, act like one and live right, you ajumma. Where do you get off casually running your mouth about someone else’s precious child?”

decisions.reason: 마지막 한 방 is the fragment “The final blow,” not a spelled-out “That was.”
Removes the old first-position goshiwon note so ajumma can be [^1].
Ajumma is the first footnoted term, so it is [^1].
Restores the goshiwon note as [^2] at first actual use.
